$comment: Single source of truth for the ai-workspace plugin marketplace. Edit this file, then run `python3 scripts/plugins.py sync` to render the per-agent manifests (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json for Claude Code, .agents/plugins/marketplace.json for Codex). Never hand-edit the rendered files: scripts/plugins.py check fails on drift. `renames` lists marketplaces this one supersedes; the installer retires them (and any plugin installed from them) so a rename never leaves a duplicate.

marketplace.name: ai-workspace
marketplace.description: David's shared AI workspace: cross-agent plugins that work identically in Claude Code and Codex.

plugins.name: obsidian-memory
plugins.description: Shared, bounded Obsidian vault memory for Codex and Claude Code.

codex.shortDescription: Shared durable memory backed by Obsidian.
codex.longDescription: Loads a bounded recent-context view from an Obsidian vault and provides a safe workflow for recalling and persisting durable project knowledge.
defaultPrompt: Recall relevant context from my Obsidian memory.
Persist this decision in my Obsidian vault.
Show the open tasks related to this project.

plugins.name: codex-pair
plugins.description: Codex CLI as Claude Code's independent second model: grounded judgment, product shaping, adversarial plan and diff review, and a technical-lead loop where Codex scopes and signs off while Claude implements.

codex.shortDescription: Independent product shaping, technical leadership, and review for Claude Code.
codex.longDescription: Runs Codex as a persistent per-branch thread in one of five read-only roles: grounded second opinion, product-and-technical shaping, adversarial plan review, technical lead that authors a bounded slice spec and later reviews the diff against it, and adversarial diff review. Claude Code remains the outer loop and sole code author; Codex supplies independent scope, challenge, and sign-off.
defaultPrompt: Scope the next slice as tech lead, then review my diff against that spec.
Shape the smallest product slice worth building before we plan implementation.
Red-team this implementation plan against the actual code.
Give me a grounded second opinion — here is my position, attack it.

plugins.name: chatgpt-consult
plugins.description: Bounded project consultations through ChatGPT web, with local MCP context, structured results, and explicit publishing.

codex.shortDescription: Consult ChatGPT web with bounded project context.
codex.longDescription: Creates project-scoped consultation requests, hands them to ChatGPT web through a safe MCP bridge, retrieves structured results, and publishes only when explicitly requested.
defaultPrompt: Consult ChatGPT web about this decision using only the files I name.
Ask my ChatGPT Project to review this diff and report the result.
Continue the last ChatGPT consultation with this follow-up.
